_comment: Per-service sync config. URLs built at runtime from .env. STRATEGY (sync_strategy): 'date' (default) = chunk historical backfill on history_field and run incremental on incremental_field — use when the table has a usable date; 'full_refresh' = re-pull the WHOLE table every run and upsert — use when the table has NO timestamp and no monotonic key (reference/lines tables); see _new_table_templates below. PRIMARY KEY (primary_key) may be a single name OR a list for a composite key — lines/detail tables MUST use a composite key (e.g. [Document_No, Line_No]) because the document number repeats across line rows. incremental_is_datetime=true if incremental_field is a datetime (e.g. SystemCreatedAt). lookback_days = trailing re-scan buffer for date incremental. API (api): 'odata' (default) = legacy ODataV4 web service published from a BC page; 'v2.0' = standard Business Central API v2.0 entity set (what Power BI's BC connector reads) - name is the camelCase entitySet (e.g. customers), primary_key is 'id', incremental on lastModifiedDateTime with incremental_is_datetime=true. incremental_extra_fields = additional date fields each re-scanned in their own pass with the same floor (BC refuses OR across distinct fields), for ledgers whose rows change after posting.

_new_table_templates._page_size_note: Optional per-service "max_page_size" overrides BC_MAXPAGESIZE (default 5000) in the Prefer: odata.maxpagesize header. BC caps it at 20000. Raise it only for NARROW rows - cost is bytes, not rows: 10000 rows of Customer Item Reference is 2.8 MB, 10000 rows of Posted_Sales_Invoice_Excel is 38 MB. A page that times out is re-fetched whole, so a big page on a wide table makes every retry expensive.

services._NOTE: Sales lines subpage of Sales_Return_Order_Excel. Unposted -> mutable. Switched from full_refresh to date-incremental on Shipment_Date: full_refresh re-upserted all 305k rows every 2h, which churned ~3.7M dead tuples/day and took the table from 206MB to 456MB. Shipment_Date is the only populated date this page exposes (no Document_Date, no SystemCreatedAt/ModifiedAt). TRADE-OFF: edits to lines shipped longer ago than lookback_days are no longer picked up; a 90d window covers ~10% of rows per run instead of 100%. Deletions were never propagated under full_refresh either (it only ever upserts), so nothing is lost there. incremental_include_undated keeps BC's 0001-01-01 blank-date lines reachable - ~11.4k rows that a bare 'ge' filter would never fetch.
services.name: Sales_Return_Order_ExcelSalesLines

services._NOTE: Posted sales credit memo lines. PK is Document_No + No (item/account number) as configured. Lines with no No carry no product data and are not wanted: quarantine_missing_pk=false drops them quietly rather than refilling quarantine/ every run and pinning the service at partial_failure. Dropped counts show as skipped=N in the run summary. This page exposes NO date field of any kind, so sync_strategy is series_key: posted documents are immutable and their numbers only grow within a BC no.-series (26CNMUM-00001 ...), so 'above the highest number stored' is a complete window. One request per series - BC answers 501 to an OR of AND-groups - and 501 to 'not (...)', so new series are learned from series_source (the parent document table, which syncs by date) instead of from the API. Narrow rows (693 B/row -> 6.9 MB/page; 322k rows), so max_page_size 10000 rather than the 5000 default.
services.name: Posted_Sales_Credit_Memo_Lines_Excel

services._NOTE: Customer Ledger Entries (page 25). ~308k rows, all from 2024-04-01 onwards. Entries are MUTABLE after posting: Open / Remaining_Amount / Closed_at_Date change when a payment is applied. No SystemCreatedAt/ModifiedAt on this page, so incremental runs a Posting_Date lookback (new/back-dated postings) plus an extra pass on Closed_at_Date (old invoices that just got closed). Partial applications that leave an old entry open are only refreshed by a --mode full run.
